Tipping Points under Detection Feedback

Source: R/feedback_sensitivity.R
feedback_tipping.Rd

Finds how much detection feedback it takes to overturn a statement about the population size.

Usage

feedback_tipping(
  x,
  threshold = NULL,
  group = NULL,
  hypothesis = NULL,
  level = 0.95
)

# S3 method for class 'uncounted_feedback_tipping'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

x

An "uncounted_feedback" object.

threshold

A single value for a group total. Use with group. The tested direction is the side of the threshold on which the estimate lies at \(\delta = 0\).

group

Group label for threshold. Defaults to "Total" when available, or the only group.

hypothesis

A comparison in the xi[...] syntax of hypotheses_popsize, such as "xi[year == 2024] - xi[year == 2019] > 0". The filters refer to the by variables of x.

level

Level of the one-sided bootstrap test: the statement is supported at \(\delta\) when the 1 - level quantile of the replicate contrasts is above 0 (for >), or the level quantile is below 0 (for <). For =, both tails use (1 - level) / 2.

...

Ignored.

Value

An object of class "uncounted_feedback_tipping", a list with statement, alternative, baseline (the contrast at \(\delta = 0\)), point and test (each c(negative, positive), NA when not reached), supported_at_zero (NA without a bootstrap), admissible_range, and curve, a data frame with delta, contrast, lower, upper and supported.

Details

Two kinds of tipping point are reported on each side of 0, within the delta_grid of x:

  • point: the \(\delta\) nearest 0 at which the point estimate of the contrast changes sign, found exactly between grid points.

  • test: with a bootstrap, the grid value nearest 0 at which the test stops supporting the statement.

If the test does not support the statement at \(\delta = 0\), there is nothing to overturn: test is NA and supported_at_zero is FALSE. Tipping points are reported whether or not they are admissible, with the admissible range shown alongside.

See also

feedback_sensitivity, hypotheses_popsize
